title: PIM for Active Directory: NAT gateway egress for the hybrid worker VM (no public IP)
purpose: Puts the hybrid worker VM's outbound traffic behind a NAT gateway and makes sure the VM itself has no public IP address.
whenToRun: Run for you by New-PimHybridWorkerInfra.ps1 (-Egress NatGateway). Run it yourself to migrate a worker built with a public IP on its VM, or to verify the egress. Azure VM worker only.

runAs.name: Network Contributor
runAs.why: creates the NAT gateway and its public IP, detaches a public IP from the VM's NIC, updates the subnet

changes.object: NAT gateway natgw-<vm> (Standard) and, when no address can be reused, the Standard static public IP pip-<vm> as its outbound address
changes.why: outbound only; nothing can connect in
changes.undo: detach it from the subnet, then delete the NAT gateway and its public IP

changes.object: a public IP on it is DETACHED (the address is kept and becomes the NAT gateway's)
changes.why: the worker is Tier 0: never a public IP of its own

changes.object: natGateway = the NAT gateway; defaultOutboundAccess = false
changes.why: outbound through the NAT gateway only
changes.undo: remove the NAT gateway from the subnet

parameters.name: TenantId
parameters.help: The tenant; the script refuses a subscription in another one.

parameters.name: Location
parameters.help: Region for the NAT gateway and its IP.

parameters.name: PublicIpName
parameters.help: The NAT gateway's public IP name (when none is reused).

readsOnly: the subnet, the VM and its NICs, the NAT gateway and public IP (read-before-write), and at the end a verification that no public IP is left on the VM
network: management.azure.com (ARM REST) and login.microsoftonline.com -- browser sign-in or an Invardia support session; no Azure CLI, no PowerShell module
whatIf: Prints the NAT gateway, the detach and the subnet change it would make; changes nothing (and, before the subnet exists, says so instead of failing).
undo: Remove the NAT gateway from the subnet, delete the NAT gateway and its public IP. A detached public IP is not re-attached to the VM (by design).
